research_domain_title: Essential Systems: Banking, Insurance, Healthcare, and Preventive Design
note: Major website and research architecture for essential industries. System-design framing — not conclusions of inherent corruption. No invented healthcare, banking, or insurance statistics. Detailed reforms blocked until sourced diagnosis modules exist.
framing_rule: Begin with system design and incentive analysis, not with conclusions such as inherent corruption. Ask what incentives produce outcomes that do not align well with the public interest, and how those incentives can be redesigned.

constitutional_question.text: How should a society design essential systems so that private innovation and investment are rewarded while the public interest remains protected?

role_in_philosophy: Banking, insurance, healthcare, and related essential industries belong in Constitutional Capitalism as systems to be designed and measured — using the same constitutional question — rather than as special cases or predetermined villains.

chapter_method.title: Essential Systems inquiry
chapter_method.summary: Rather than beginning with proposed reforms, each essential-system chapter answers four questions so readers reason through evidence with the project.

questions.text: What is this system supposed to accomplish?
Where are the incentives well aligned, and where are they not?
What reforms would better align the system with the principles of Constitutional Capitalism?

systems.title: Banking
systems.purpose: Safeguard deposits, provide credit, finance businesses, facilitate payments, and support homeownership — serving the real economy.

principle.text: The financial system should primarily reward the creation of productive value rather than the extraction of value.

design_questions: Should more lending remain local through community banks and credit unions?
How do we encourage financing for productive investment rather than primarily speculative activity?
Should mergers face greater scrutiny when they reduce competition?
How do we increase transparency around fees and lending practices?
How do we expand access to capital for entrepreneurs and rural communities?
systems.note: Not whether banking should exist — how to ensure it serves the real economy. Research before detailed banking legislation.

systems.title: Insurance
systems.purpose: Spread risk while balancing affordable premiums, adequate coverage, financial stability, fair claims handling, and innovation.
design_questions: Are incentives aligned with long-term prevention?
How can fraud be reduced without making legitimate claims harder?
Should communities receive incentives for reducing risks through safer infrastructure and preventive health?
systems.method_note: Compare regulatory models and measure outcomes rather than assuming one answer.
systems.note: Architecture and research questions only — no invented denial or premium statistics.

systems.title: Healthcare
systems.purpose: Treat illness and help people remain healthy — recognizing healthy citizens as one of society's greatest strengths.
systems.foundational_idea: Healthy citizens are not simply beneficiaries of society — they are one of its greatest strengths.

principle.text: A constitutional republic should measure success not only by how well it treats illness, but by how well it helps people remain healthy.

health_maintenance_investments: vaccination where appropriate and supported by evidence
systems.note: Shift from a system focused primarily on treating illness to one that also invests heavily in maintaining health. Evidence required before policy packages.

systems.title: Pharmaceuticals
systems.purpose: Discover, develop, and deliver treatments that improve and extend lives while preserving innovation incentives and improving affordability and access.
systems.framing_caution: Do not assert broad claims such as 'the system is designed to keep people sick' without strong evidence. Prefer researchable incentive questions.
design_questions: Are current incentives weighted more toward treatment than prevention?
How should society encourage research into prevention, cures, and rare diseases?
How can drug pricing be more transparent?
How should publicly funded research affect later pricing or access?
How do we preserve incentives for innovation while improving affordability?
systems.note: Acknowledge life-extending treatments and examine financial incentives rigorously.

community_health_index.name: Community Health Index
community_health_index.summary: Every community could publish a Community Health Index so places compete to become the healthiest to live — not merely to host the biggest hospital.
community_health_index.note: Design agenda — do not invent index scores or community rankings.

preventive_society.goal: Shift public investment gradually from paying for avoidable crises toward preventing those crises in the first place.
preventive_society.measurement_note: Prevention often produces benefits that are difficult to see because they are problems that never occur, but those benefits can still be measured.

essential_systems_test.title: Essential Systems Test
essential_systems_test.purpose: Evaluate major industries and essential systems with the same questions before accepting reforms into the framework.

questions.text: Does this industry create long-term value?
Are consumers able to make informed choices?
Are incentives aligned with the public good?
Are profits earned through innovation and service, or primarily through barriers to competition or information asymmetry?
Are communities stronger because this industry exists?
Is the system transparent and accountable?
Are risks and rewards fairly distributed?
Does the industry invest in the people and places that make its success possible?
Can the public measure whether the system is actually improving lives?

research_status.next: Phase 2.1: source FDIC/Fed banking structure, NAIC/state insurance competition series, CDC/NCHS health outcomes, and pharmaceutical pricing/transparency literature without asserting unsupported systemic intent claims
